column1: # open-agent-robot — every markdown document under `docs/`, with its status and what
# overturned it.
# Why this file exists, from a measurement rather than a principle: on 2026-08-25 there
# were six research rounds and one design critique in `docs/` — 191 KiB together — and
# **four of the six carried no supersession marker of any kind**. One of the four is
# round 4, whose §0 build order `docs/design-critique-memory-safety-2026-08-22.md` §4
# explicitly replaces, and whose memory pick `docs/research-round5-memory-safety-2026-08-22.md`
# re-answers in its own header. A reader who opened round 4 first had no way to learn
# either fact. The rounds are kept verbatim on purpose (they are measured evidence), so
# the retraction has to live somewhere outside them, and "somewhere" has to be a place a
# machine checks.
# `infra/doc_status.py` walks `docs/**/*.md` **recursively** and checks this table in both
# directions. The recursion is not cosmetic: `docs/evidence/` holds two documents, and a
# non-recursive glob would have exempted that whole directory while reporting clean.
# Same shape as `infra/graph_gaps.tsv`, `infra/dormant_seams.tsv`,
# `infra/standalone_entrypoints.tsv` and `infra/generated_paths.tsv`, and for the same
# reason: an excuse living inside the guard is where the next unreviewed exemption gets
# added. A document on disk with no row here is a finding (**a new document cannot join
# `docs/` silently**). A row whose file no longer exists is also a finding — a stale row
# would quietly cover the next document that arrives with the same name.
# Columns (tab-separated):  path <TAB> status <TAB> relation <TAB> reason
# `status` is a closed set, checked by the guard:
#   current     the answer to "what is true now". A reader may cite it as the design.
#   evidence    kept verbatim because it is a dated measurement. It may be cited for
#               *how a number was obtained*, never for what the design currently is.
#   superseded  wholly replaced. The relation must name the replacement. This class is
#               the one that should stay empty: nothing in this tree has been wholly
#               replaced yet, because the rounds are evidence and evidence does not
#               expire — only conclusions drawn from it do. If a row ever lands here,
#               deleting the file becomes a reviewable question rather than a habit.
# `relation` is `-`, or one or more terms joined by `;`, each from a closed vocabulary:
#   superseded_by:<path>            everything this document concluded now lives there.
#   overturned_in_part_by:<path>    some conclusion here is dead; the rest still stands.
# **The `;` is load-bearing, and it came from the data.** A single-value column looked
# sufficient until round 4 turned out to have *two* independent overturners — the
# critique replaced its build order and round 5 re-answered its memory pick — and rounds
# 1–2 likewise have two. A one-slot column would have forced dropping one of each pair,
# which is precisely the flattening `docs/design.md` §7 exists to prevent: the row would
# have read as complete while hiding half of what a reader needs.
# Every `<path>` a relation names must exist and must itself be `current` or `evidence`.
# A retraction that points at a superseded document is a dead end with a footnote.
# `reason` must be at least 60 characters. The floor is the same judgement as
# `infra/graph_gaps.tsv`: a reason short enough to be a shrug is not a reason, and the
# whole value of a reviewable exemption is that someone had to write down why.
# `docs/INDEX.md` is the human-readable rendering of this table. The guard checks the two
# against each other in both directions, because two readers of one set of facts each
# stay green while the other side moves — the same rule that keeps `README.md` and
# `README.zh-TW.md` in one PR.
docs/INDEX.md
column4: the human-readable rendering of this table; it exists so that a reader lands on the status list before opening any round, and the guard checks the two against each other in both directions

column1: docs/workflow.md
column4: the sequence charts, drawn as the counterpart to docs/architecture.svg's standing shape: what happens in order when someone speaks, interrupts, asks to be forgotten, or triggers a tool

column4: the agent-brain round; the critique §4 explicitly replaces its §0 build order, and round 5's header states that its cognee + Graphiti memory pick rested on the weakest evidence in it and re-answers the question
